units.text: Apple Finally Shares tvOS 27 Release Notes With List of New Features

Apple today finally shared release notes for tvOS 27, nearly two weeks after releasing the software update. Many of the new features and changes listed were already known, but we are sharing the notes for the sake of completeness.

tvOS 27 was released on Monday, September 14, but the Apple TV does not show release notes for software updates in the Settings app. Instead, Apple periodically updates a support document outlining what is new in tvOS updates.

Here is what is new for the Apple TV on tvOS 27, including video podcasts in the Podcasts app, AutoMix in the Apple Music app, the ability to set your preferred text size across supported apps, improved AirPlay performance, and more:

This update brings enhancements to the Apple Music, Podcasts, and AirPlay experiences on tvOS. It also brings captions to more content, adds the ability to block individual apps, and provides bug fixes and security updates for your Apple TV 4K.
Apple Music
- Hi-Res Lossless audio support provides a studio-quality listening experience.
- AutoMix transitions one song into the next like a DJ does, time stretching and beatmatching to deliver a continuous playback experience.
This release also includes other features and improvements:
- Video podcasts bring your favorite shows to the TV in the redesigned Podcasts app.
- AirPlay performance improvements deliver faster, more responsive connections when sharing photos, videos, and music from iPhone, iPad, or Mac to Apple TV.
- Transcribed audio helps you follow along with content when standard captions or subtitles aren't provided.
- Dynamic Text support in Accessibility settings allows you to set your preferred text size across supported apps.
- Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.
tvOS 27 is compatible with the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and newer.

evidence.discovery_title: Leaks reveal a new Apple HomePod mini, iPad mini, and Apple TV 4K
evidence.raw_lead: Apple’s not done with hardware announcements this year.
evidence.title: Leaks reveal a new Apple HomePod mini, iPad mini, and Apple TV 4K

units.text: Apple is expected to announce more hardware before the end of the year following the debut of the iPhone 18 Pro and folding iPhone Duo earlier this month. The updated products will include a new version of the HomePod mini, the iPad mini 8, and the Apple TV 4K, according to details and images discovered in Apple’s own code by MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris.

Details from the leaks are sparse, but the HomePod Mini 2 will carry forward a similar design to the original model that debuted in late 2020. While the current model is available in bright color options including orange, yellow, and blue, the leaked images of the HomePod Mini 2 reveal new green, pink, blue, white, and black shades that are more subdued and better suited to blending into existing decor.

The new iPad mini 8 will replace the seventh-generation model that launched two years ago with an upgrade from Apple’s A17 Pro chip to the recently announced A20 Pro found in the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. The leaked images only show the front of the iPad mini 8, but Apple has moved its front-facing camera to the landscape edge of the tablet, while a groove on the top edge of the display, similar to the iPhone’s, seems to indicate an added speaker.

As previously reported by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the next version of the iPad could also include improved waterproofing thanks to a new vibration-based speaker, and an OLED display like the larger iPad Pro features.

The current version of the Apple TV is nearly four years old, but today’s leaks don’t give much away about what upgrades the new 4th generation version will include aside from a very similar design to its predecessor. Previous details uncovered by MacRumors’ Perris include a potential upgrade to Apple’s A17 Pro chip, while in 2024 Mark Gurman said the next Apple TV would use Apple’s in-house Bluetooth and Wi-Fi chip we now know as the N1.

units.text: 苹果即将推出的新一代Apple TV 4K再次传出重要消息。最新泄露的信息显示，这款已经多年未更新的流媒体设备将迎来近年来最大幅度的硬件升级，不仅将获得A19系列处理器，还有望成为苹果人工智能和智能家居生态的重要组成部分。
根据最新曝光的系统代码，新款Apple TV对应的设备标识指向A19系列芯片架构。这意味着苹果可能为其配备A19或A19 Pro处理器，而不再采用此前外界普遍猜测的A17 Pro方案。
如果该消息属实，新产品的性能提升幅度将相当明显。现行Apple TV 4K于2022年发布，搭载A15仿生芯片和4GB内存。而A19系列处理器不仅拥有更先进的制造工艺和更强的运算能力，同时也意味着新设备有望配备8GB甚至12GB内存，为人工智能功能运行提供必要硬件支持。
业内人士认为，苹果之所以为Apple TV引入如此高规格芯片，一个重要原因是为即将到来的新一代Siri和Apple Intelligence功能做准备。
近年来，苹果持续推进设备端人工智能战略，而客厅设备被视为未来家庭AI生态的重要节点。新款Apple TV预计将支持更加智能的Siri功能，使用户能够通过自然语言完成内容搜索、家庭控制以及更多跨设备操作。
除处理器升级外，新设备还预计搭载苹果自研N1无线网络芯片。这款芯片有望支持Wi‑Fi 7标准，在无线带宽、延迟和稳定性方面带来明显改善，对于4K乃至未来更高规格流媒体内容传输具有重要意义。
与此同时，苹果还可能同步更新Siri Remote遥控器。虽然具体改动尚未曝光，但相关代码已经出现新遥控器的迹象，显示苹果正在对用户交互体验进行调整。
值得注意的是，苹果似乎并不打算彻底改变产品外观设计。根据目前曝光的信息，新款Apple TV 4K将继续采用现有的方形黑色机身设计，整体体积和外观变化预计非常有限，升级重点主要集中在内部硬件。
分析师指出，新款Apple TV承担的角色已经不只是流媒体播放器。随着Apple Intelligence、HomeKit、Matter和Thread生态不断扩展，Apple TV正逐渐成为Apple Intelligence家庭系统中的控制中心。
更强大的处理器和更大的内存容量，也让它具备承担本地AI计算、智能家居协调以及轻量级游戏设备等多重任务的能力。
事实上，市场原本预计苹果会在2025年更新Apple TV产品线，但相关计划最终延后。因此，2026版Apple TV 4K距离上一代产品发布已经接近四年时间，成为Apple产品线中更新周期最长的设备之一。
随着泄露信息不断增加，外界普遍认为新设备已经接近正式发布阶段。如果苹果最终为其配备A19或A19 Pro芯片，那么这将成为Apple TV历史上性能提升幅度最大的一次升级，同时也意味着苹果正进一步将电视、智能家居和人工智能服务整合到统一生态之中。

units.text: iOS 27 brings a variety of new features to Apple Wallet, including one exclusive to Apple Card that I wish every card offered: a hub for all recurring transactions.
iOS 27 shows Apple Card recurring transactions in one place, making it easy to track subscriptions
Subscriptions are increasingly popular in the digital-centric world. As such, it can be easy to lose track of everything you’re subscribed to.

While plenty of apps and services offer to keep track of your subscriptions, giving third parties access to your financial info can spark privacy concerns. Fortunately, those solutions soon won’t be needed for Apple Card.
In iOS 27, the Wallet app offers a new feature for Apple Card users: a recurring transaction section.
When viewing your Apple Card in iOS 27, there’s a new ‘Recurring’ option inside the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
Tapping this will show you a list of upcoming recurring transactions, and even lets you see them on a monthly calendar view.
I like to think I have a pretty good sense of all the things I’m subscribed to. But that takes effort. And Apple Card’s new feature makes tracking subscriptions pretty effortless.
I’m especially a fan of the calendar view, as it’s so nice getting to see at a glance exactly when each charge is expected to go through.

iOS 27 lists recurring transactions based on your Apple Card history, so it won’t always catch everything. The Wallet app has a disclaimer that states: “Dates and amounts shown are predicted based on your transaction history and may not be exact. Routine spending may incorrectly appear as recurring.”
If you do see an item that’s incorrectly marked as recurring, it’s easy to correct the error.
I really hope Apple Card inspires more credit cards and banks to copy iOS 27’s new feature. It feels like a no-brainer addition that every card should have.
Now I want to start moving all my subscriptions on to Apple Card.

units.text: Apple Music has announced which eight artists will be performing first at the new Apple Music Hall in London, beginning with Elton John on September 28, 2026.

Days after unveiling its spectacular new live concert venue in London, Apple Music has begun programming the venue. It's announced eight artists playing from September to the start of December, with ticketing starting shortly, assuming you can navigate the website.
Apple Music Hall's guide to forthcoming shows is stylish, dynamic, and looks brilliant as you scroll through the whole page. It's just more of a pain when you try to select any of them.
Fortunately, you have time. While Elton John opens the program with a concert on September 28, 2026, tickets are not on sale until that morning.

That's a little unusual and realistically limits who can get to the performance at London's Battersea Power Station. Apple is also releasing tickets on that date for the next two artists, who are playing on October 2 and October 7 respectively.
Once you get through to this section, buying tickets will be easy. But the program you have to go through first is a little tricky to navigate - image credit: Apple.
The first artists at Apple Music Hall, and when they are performing, are:
Elton John: September 28
Baby Keem: October 2
Skye Newman: October 7
Troye Sivan: October 13
Arlo Parks: October 22
Burna Boy: October 29
Chase & Status: November 26
Charli XCC: December 2

Doors for the first three concerts open at 6:00 P.M. local time each and it's likely that all of them will. Each concert appears to have only a single pricing tier, which is 40 pounds Sterling, or approximately $53.
The hall can seat 600 people. During its announcement of the Apple Music Hall, Apple said that therefore an artist could play an intimate set.

However, it also said that because of the audio, spatial audio, video, and live streaming capabilities of the space, they could simultaneously create a finished broadcast-quality recording. While Apple has not announced this, it's beyond likely that all of these concerts will be made available on Apple Music at some point.

The opening programme is commendably broad, but it's fitting that Elton John opens it. That's because he was also one of the first DJs when Apple first began its radio station streaming with Beats 1 in 2015.

evidence.raw_lead: Take full advantage of the iPhone 18 Pro’s new camera.
evidence.title: These camera apps give you more control over the iPhone 18 Pro’s aperture

units.text: One of the questionable limitations of the iPhone 18 Pro’s new main camera with a variable aperture is that you’re limited to just four settings in the native iOS’ camera app in manual mode: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4. Those same limitations are also in place when the app is adjusting the iris itself in Auto aperture mode, but it turns out that’s not a strict limitation of the iPhone’s camera hardware. Apple’s SDK allows third-party camera apps to implement more granular control of the aperture.

BlackMagic Design’s well-featured and still completely free BlackMagic Camera app for iOS was one of the first third-party options to introduce support for the iPhone 18 Pro’s adjustable aperture. But instead of just four stop settings, the app offers 10 presets with additional options in-between the settings available in iOS’ camera. The iPhoneographers YouTube channel tested the new functionality in version 3.5 of the app last week and while they describe it as “pretty buggy” the app has since been updated to version 3.5.1 with “general performance and stability improvements.”

Yesterday, Moment followed suit with an announcement on X that its $12.99 Moment Pro Camera II app has also been updated to support the iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture. You can adjust the aperture from f/1.48 to f/4.0 in 1/3 stop increments giving you 10 presets like Blackmagic’s app, which is the same approach as most digital cameras take. Given the small sensor size of the iPhone 18 Pro you may be hard-pressed to see a difference in background blur and focus depth when comparing photos with f-stops different by just 1/3 of a stop, but more control is never a bad thing.

units.text: 快科技9月26日消息，苹果入门级iPad终于要支棱起来了，日前，iPad 12关键参数曝光，新机将在芯片、内存和网络等方面迎来升级。
据MacRumors报道，其撰稿人Aaron Perris通过挖掘苹果内部代码发现，iPad 12将配备A19芯片、8GB内存、N1网络芯片以及C1X调制解调器。
作为对比，目前在售的iPad 11搭载A16芯片和6GB内存。
升级至A19和8GB内存后，iPad 12不仅性能将进一步提升，也将具备运行Apple Intelligence及新一代Siri AI功能的硬件基础。
网络方面，iPad 12将搭载苹果自研N1网络芯片，支持Wi-Fi 7、蓝牙6以及Thread（智能家居通信协议）。
蜂窝版本则将采用苹果C1X基带，支持Sub-6GHz 5G网络，相比现款iPad所使用的高通基带，C1X在能效方面有望进一步改善。
外观设计上，目前尚未出现明显改动信息，新机预计仍将延续现款整体设计，不过不排除增加新的机身配色。
作为参考，现款iPad 11起售价2999元，配备11英寸IPS LCD屏，分辨率为2360x1640，采用USB-C接口，不支持Apple Intelligence。
从现有爆料来看，iPad 12的升级重点将集中在芯片、内存以及AI能力上，屏幕等基础规格预计仍会保持入门级产品定位。

units.text: 尽管苹果持续提高iPhone售价，但在印度市场，这种涨价策略似乎并未削弱消费者热情。最新市场数据显示，随着iPhone进一步强化其高端和身份象征属性，苹果正在印度获得越来越强劲的市场表现。
根据市场调研数据，iPhone 18 Pro上市后在印度的需求明显高于上一代产品。目前，iPhone 18 Pro的市场需求较2025年同期的iPhone 17 Pro增长接近20%。这一增长发生在产品价格进一步上调之后，因此受到市场广泛关注。
市场研究机构Counterpoint Research认为，苹果在印度智能手机市场的份额有望在2026年达到10%。如果这一预测实现，将是苹果首次在印度单个自然年度内获得两位数市场份额。相比之下，苹果在2022年的市场份额仅约4%。
9月18日iPhone 18系列正式开售当天，印度多个主要城市的苹果零售店迎来大批消费者。部分消费者专程从外地赶往门店购买新机，还有人在门店外排队超过十小时，希望能够第一时间获得产品。
值得注意的是，推动销售增长的主要原因并不完全来自新功能。
从消费者反馈来看，很多购买者更加在意拥有“最新款iPhone”本身，而不是新机增加了哪些技术特性。对于不少用户而言，iPhone已经超越普通消费电子产品范畴，成为一种身份、品位和社会地位的象征。而价格上涨反而进一步强化了这种高端形象。
分析人士认为，这与印度消费市场近年来出现的“高端化”趋势密切相关。越来越多中高收入消费者愿意在具有品牌价值和社会象征意义的产品上投入更多资金，而苹果正成为这一趋势的重要受益者。
与此同时，苹果也通过金融服务降低了消费者的购买门槛。
虽然基础版iPhone 18 Pro在印度售价约合1700美元，但苹果提供的零利率分期付款计划，使消费者能够以较低月供完成购买。在部分方案下，用户只需每月支付设备价格不到十分之一的金额即可获得新手机，大大缓解了一次性付款压力。
事实上，苹果在印度市场的发展势头已经持续多年。虽然公司在2026年第二季度曾出现销量下滑，但业内普遍认为主要原因是供应不足，而非市场需求减弱。从整体趋势来看，苹果在印度的销售增长已经连续保持了约四年时间。
与苹果形成鲜明对比的是，部分主攻入门级智能手机市场的厂商正面临销售压力。随着消费者消费能力提升以及品牌升级趋势增强，低端智能手机市场增长明显放缓，一些厂商销量甚至出现明显下滑。
不过，业内人士也提醒，高端消费热潮未必会永远持续。如果苹果未来无法维持其品牌吸引力，或者消费者对于高价产品的接受度发生变化，那么这种增长势头可能受到影响。同时，中国手机品牌不断向高端市场发起冲击，也可能在未来与苹果展开更加激烈的竞争。
尽管如此，从目前市场表现来看，价格上涨不仅没有阻碍印度消费者购买iPhone，反而进一步强化了产品的高端定位。在当下的印度市场，iPhone正逐渐从一款智能手机演变为一种具有象征意义的消费品，而这种属性正在帮助苹果持续扩大其市场影响力。

units.text: New Apple TV 4K Leaked

MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris has uncovered an image file from Apple for an unreleased Apple TV 4K, suggesting that a new model will finally be released soon. The image is specifically for an "Apple TV 4K (4th generation)" model.
Apple TV 4K (4th generation) image (on a gradient)

The image reveals that the Apple TV will have the same external design as the current model, with all of its upgrades expected to be internal. Rumored features include an A17 Pro chip or newer, an increased 8GB of RAM, Apple Intelligence and Siri AI support, an Apple-designed N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 support, and a revised Siri Remote.
The current Apple TV is nearly four years old, having been announced in October 2022. It is equipped with an A15 Bionic chip and 4GB of RAM.
With an A17 Pro chip or newer, the next Apple TV will have faster performance and hardware-accelerated ray tracing for improved graphics rendering in games.
With the N1 chip, the Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

Wi-Fi 7 has increased bandwidth, in part because it allows for data transmission over the 2.4GHz, 5GHz, and 6GHz bands simultaneously with a supported device and router. Wi-Fi 7 is theoretically up to 4× faster than the current Apple TV's Wi-Fi 6, but real-world speeds are bottlenecked by internet service providers and other factors.

Siri AI will likely be the headline new feature on the next Apple TV, with tvOS 27 expected to gain a Siri app on the device. units.text: iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes.
iOS 27 lets you import physical passes, membership cards, event tickets into Apple Wallet
Apple Wallet offers a host of features to help you replace your physical wallet and keys.
It holds credit cards, driver’s licenses, transit cards, boarding passes, event tickets, car keys, home keys, hotel keys, and more.
And with iOS 27, the Wallet app takes another big step toward being the only wallet you need.
That’s because you can now import physical passes, tickets, membership cards, and the like into Apple Wallet.
Here’s how it works, per Apple:

iPhone and Apple Watch users will be able to create and store passes in Apple Wallet from physical cards, like loyalty or membership cards, eliminating the need to fumble through pockets and bags. Users can also create and add a pass directly from Apple Wallet. Once added, passes are ready to present as a barcode or QR code right from their iPhone or Apple Watch.
Digital passes are a lot more common today than when Apple Wallet first launched. But they aren’t available for everything.

I definitely still encounter businesses and events that utilize physical passes exclusively. And when I do, it adds a little anxiety to my life because I then need to remember to bring those passes with me at the right time.
But with iOS 27, everything can start going in the Wallet app, which is always with me. By putting everything in Wallet, the mental burden of remembering to bring something extra is suddenly gone.

units.text: An image of the new Apple TV 4K hardware appears to have leaked, showing that there's nothing new on the outside. But big changes are rumored for the inside.

The current Apple TV 4K was released in October 2022, and a new model has been rumored to be in the cards for some time. The model on store shelves today features an aging A15 Bionic chip and just 4GB of RAM.

Now, the image file reported by MacRumors has revealed the new Apple TV 4K's upgrades will all be internal, with Apple choosing to stick with its tried and tested design of a small, featureless black box.

The good news is that previous leaks have suggested it will be a box very much ready for 2027 and beyond. Rumored upgrades will make the new Apple TV 4K a more capable streaming and gaming device while bringing Siri AI to the TV for the first time.
The presence of the image file also suggests that the new Apple TV 4K will be released sooner rather than later. It was already expected to launch at some point this fall.
Much-needed upgrades

Previous Apple TV 4K rumors have pointed to some big improvements in terms of performance. The iPhone 18 Pro's A20 Pro is expected to be a huge upgrade for gamers, while a doubling of RAM to 8GB will also be beneficial for larger apps.

Both of these upgrades will also allow Apple to bring Siri AI to the Apple TV 4K. Users will be able to ask Siri questions and have it find content or launch apps with a reliability not currently offered by the ailing digital assistant.

On the connectivity front, Apple's N1 chip is set to bring super-fast Wi-Fi 7 to the Apple TV 4K for the first time. The same chip will be responsible for Bluetooth 6 support, allowing for a stronger, more reliable connection to accessories. One of those accessories is also set to be a revised Siri Remote.

One aspect of the new Apple TV 4K that remains unknown is its price. Apple hiked the price of the current model to $199 in June 2026. Streaming fans will hope for a price cut when the new model launches.

evidence.raw_lead: 科技媒体 AppleInsider 昨日（9 月 25 日）发布博文，采访了罗恩 · 约翰逊（Ron Johnson），并围绕着苹果零售店（Apple Store）等话题展开讨论。
evidence.title: 苹果零售总设计师约翰逊：Apple Store 未过时，iPhone Duo 等仍需“亲手摸、现场试”体验

units.text: IT之家 9 月 26 日消息，科技媒体 AppleInsider 昨日（9 月 25 日）发布博文，采访了罗恩 · 约翰逊（Ron Johnson），并围绕着苹果零售店（Apple Store）等话题展开讨论。
IT之家查询公开资料，约翰逊出生于 1959 年，于 2000 年被史蒂夫 · 乔布斯聘请，担任苹果零售业务高级副总裁，负责从零搭建 Apple Store，可谓是苹果零售体系真正的“总设计师”。
一、为什么苹果必须开自己的店？
约翰逊称 2000 年前后，苹果产品虽然优秀，但价格更高，且在大型零售商里常与更便宜的 PC 摆在一起，导致“有兴趣却难转化成交”。
约翰逊认为：苹果需要把“产品体验”直接带到消费者面前，用自己的空间讲述品牌故事、演示功能、提供服务（如后来的 Genius Bar），才能把关注变成购买。
二、这是一场多大的“豪赌”？
乔布斯回归时，苹果一度只剩约 30 天的现金储备；零售店是重资产、高固定成本的生意，对当时的苹果是巨大风险。
即便如此，约翰逊和乔布斯仍决定“每年开 25 家店”，四年内扩展到近 100 家，包括标志性的第五大道旗舰店。约翰逊在采访中表示，当年苹果公司别无选择，在现金流紧张下，只能豪赌数百万美元开设零售店。
三、苹果零售店成功的核心是什么？
约翰逊回忆第一次见乔布斯时惊讶于产品线只有四款，但这反而成为优势：门店不必堆货，而是留出空间让用户深度体验。
此外苹果零售店的标志性服务之一就是“天才吧”（Genius Bar），其功能定位强调“帮助而非推销”，甚至内部曾考虑叫“Geek Bar”，最终选定更能吸引顶尖人才的名称。在信息过载时代，清晰的产品叙事 + 可触达的服务，比“更多选择”更能降低决策成本。
四、为什么微软等模仿者没成功？
约翰逊指出零售之路很难，成功取决于选址、空间设计、人员素质、服务流程等综合因素，而微软未能完全复制苹果的体验内核。
五、今天还需要实体店吗？
访谈中提到：虽然发布会线上观看量巨大，但像 iPhone Duo 这类新产品，用户仍需要“亲手摸、现场试”才能理解差异。约翰逊认为，实体店并未过时，在新产品体验转化上仍不可替代。

units.text: 苹果下一代入门级平板电脑iPad 12的更多信息近日浮出水面。根据最新曝光的内部资料和供应链消息，这款产品虽然不会迎来全新的外观设计，但将在处理器、内存、无线连接以及人工智能功能方面获得近年来最重要的一次升级。
从目前披露的信息来看，iPad 12将继续沿用现有11英寸全面屏设计，整体外观与上一代产品基本保持一致。机身仍将采用铝合金结构，保留USB‑C接口、侧边Touch ID指纹识别以及现有的配件兼容体系，包括Apple Pencil等产品都将继续获得支持。
苹果此次升级的重点集中在内部配置。消息显示，iPad 12预计将搭载A18或A19系列处理器。无论最终采用哪一款芯片，都将基于更先进的3纳米工艺制造，在性能和能效方面明显领先于现款产品所使用的A16芯片。
除了处理器升级之外，内存容量也将同步提升。新机预计配备8GB内存，高于现有机型的6GB配置。这项升级看似普通，却具有重要战略意义，因为它意味着iPad 12有望成为首款支持Apple Intelligence的入门级iPad。
过去，Apple Intelligence主要依赖更高性能的芯片和更大的内存配置，因此仅限于部分高端设备使用。而在iPad 12上，苹果计划将这一人工智能体系进一步下放至大众级产品线。
分析人士认为，这将成为新机最大的卖点之一。未来用户不仅能够使用增强版Siri，还可获得AI写作辅助、内容摘要、图像生成以及各种智能生产力工具，从而让入门级iPad具备过去高端机型才拥有的人工智能能力。
无线连接方面，新款iPad也有望迎来明显提升。苹果近年来开始在部分设备中使用自研无线通信芯片N1，而最新消息显示，iPad 12可能会加入这一阵营。如果相关计划最终实现，新机将支持Wi‑Fi 7、Bluetooth 6以及Thread智能家居网络协议。
对于用户而言，这意味着更快的数据传输速度、更低的网络延迟以及更好的智能家居设备兼容能力。同时，Wi‑Fi 7还将使iPad首次能够充分利用6GHz频段网络，提高未来数年的网络适应能力。
与此同时，苹果预计不会对显示屏进行重大升级。

units.text: iPad Mini 8 Leaked: A20 Pro Chip, Landscape Camera, and More
Apple's next-generation iPad mini will feature the A20 Pro chip, a rearranged front-facing camera, and a new speaker system, leaked code reveals.

The information originates from Apple's own code (spotted by MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris) and also shows clear product images of the new ‌iPad mini‌. Although images of the device only show the front, leaving any design changes of the rear or side profile unknown, there are still visible changes.

The new ‌iPad mini‌ features a landscape front-facing camera, making it the final iPad to transition to this positioning. It also has a small groove cut out of the top of the display glass, just like the iPhone, presumably for the speaker. The volume buttons and power button remain on the top of the device.
We are not sharing the exact details of the files, but their presence in Apple's code suggests that the product is likely to launch soon.
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that the next-generation ‌iPad mini‌ will feature water resistance and an all new vibration-based speaker, so the icons appear to corroborate that claim.
The new ‌iPad mini‌ is rumored to feature a slightly larger screen, an OLED display, and more. Gurman expects it to launch by the end of October.

units.text: Apple Code Confirms iPad 12 Specs: A19, 8GB RAM, N1, C1X Modem
The next low-cost iPad will be equipped with an A19 chip, C1X modem, N1 networking chip, and 8GB RAM, according to details found in Apple's code by MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris.

We've heard some of these same specifications in prior rumors, so this is more of a confirmation than a new leak. The ‌iPad‌ 11 has an A16 chip, so the upgrade to the A19 in the 12th-generation ‌iPad‌ will bring a noticeable improvement in performance. More importantly, the A19 supports Apple Intelligence, so the ‌iPad‌ 12 will have all the ‌Apple Intelligence‌ and Siri AI features missing from the ‌iPad‌ 11.
The ‌iPad‌ 11 has 6GB RAM, but 8GB RAM is the minimum for ‌Apple Intelligence‌, and the RAM boost will also speed things up.

Apple's C1X modem supports sub–6GHz 5G networks, and it is more efficient than the Qualcomm modem used in the existing ‌iPad‌. The addition of the N1 networking chip will bring support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread.
Though not included in the code, it's possible the ‌iPad‌ 12 will be available in new colors.

There is no word on when Apple will release the new ‌iPad‌, and at this point, we're not expecting it until spring 2027. The current ‌iPad‌ is priced starting at $449 after a June 2026 price hike, and the new model will likely have the same starting price.

There's no low-cost ‌iPad‌ coming this year, but Apple is expected to refresh the iPad mini before the end of October. We discovered new details about the ‌iPad mini‌ just this morning. It will have an A20 Pro chip, a new speaker system, and a landscape front-facing camera. Prior rumors say it will feature an OLED display as the main upgrade.
We also found official images of the Apple TV 4K and the HomePod mini, including its colors. The ‌HomePod mini‌ will come in green, pink, blue, white, and black.

units.text: 苹果新一代iPad mini 8近日通过内部代码和产品资料首次曝光。这款小尺寸平板预计将在延续现有外观设计的基础上迎来核心硬件升级，并进一步强化对Apple Intelligence人工智能功能的支持。
根据目前泄露的信息，iPad mini 8整体设计不会出现重大变化。设备仍将延续现有全面屏方案、窄边框设计以及约8英寸级别的机身尺寸。苹果显然认为当前iPad mini的工业设计仍然具备竞争力，因此更新重点将主要集中在内部配置。
此次升级最受关注的部分是处理器。新机预计将采用比现款更先进的A系列芯片，以满足未来Apple Intelligence功能对于本地人工智能运算能力的需求。分析人士认为，苹果正在逐步统一旗下设备的AI体验，而iPad mini 8也将成为这一战略的重要组成部分。
目前在售的iPad mini已经成为苹果产品线中最特殊的设备之一。它兼具智能手机的便携性和传统平板电脑的显示面积，在阅读、游戏、移动办公、飞行导航、医疗应用以及教育市场拥有相对稳定的用户群体。
因此，苹果对于iPad mini产品线的更新策略一直较为谨慎。与iPad Pro或iPad Air相比，iPad mini通常不会获得激进的外观改造，而是通过性能升级来延长产品生命周期。
从曝光资料来看，iPad mini 8预计将继续保留USB-C接口，并维持对Apple Pencil的支持能力。显示屏尺寸和机身结构大概率保持不变，从而确保与现有配件生态的兼容性。
与此同时，苹果未来的重点显然已经转向人工智能功能整合。随着Apple Intelligence逐步进入更多设备，更强大的神经网络运算能力将成为新一代硬件的重要卖点。对于iPad mini而言，这意味着它不仅是一台小尺寸平板，还将成为能够运行本地人工智能任务的移动计算设备。
业内人士认为，尽管外观变化有限，但性能和AI能力的提升将成为推动用户升级的主要动力。特别是在越来越多应用开始整合生成式人工智能功能的背景下，小尺寸平板也正在从单纯的内容消费设备转变为更加全面的生产力工具。
目前苹果尚未正式公布iPad mini 8的发布时间和完整规格信息。但随着产品资料开始出现在内部系统中，外界普遍预计这款设备已经接近发布阶段。
对于喜欢小尺寸平板的用户而言，iPad mini 8的到来意味着苹果并未放弃这一独特产品类别。相反，在人工智能时代的背景下，iPad mini正被重新赋予新的定位，而新一代机型也有望成为苹果移动AI生态中的重要一环。

evidence.title: Higher prices are just making iPhones more desirable premium in India

units.text: Far from hurting sales, raising iPhone prices has brought Apple growing market share in India, at least for now, and at least while it also has installment plans.

Analysts have predictably yet plausibly argued that higher iPhone prices and no base iPhone 18 would hit Apple's bottom line. That may well be true in most places, but a new CNBC report says it definitely is not in India.

Reportedly, the iPhone 18 Pro is seeing almost 20% more demand in the country than the iPhone 17 Pro at this point in 2025. "Apple's volume market share is likely to hit 10% in 2026," said Counterpoint Research director Tarun Pathak, "reaching double digits in a single calendar year for the first time, up from 4% in 2022."

On September 18 when the new models were released, customers traveled for hours to buy them at the Apple Stores in major cities such as Mumbai. Once there, some are said to have waited in line for up to ten hours.

Significantly, the demand is apparently not linked to the new features of the iPhone 18 Pro. Based on comments from customers at the Apple Stores, what mattered much more was simply owning the latest iPhone.
The now higher prices are affirming the iPhone as a premium and so aspirational smartphone. This Indian "premiumization" is not limited to smartphones, but Apple is benefiting from it.

And Apple is helping the situation through providing various financing offers. The base iPhone 18 Pro costs the equivalent of $1,700 in India, but zero-interest payment programs mean buyers can pay under 10% per month for a year.
Only Apple is benefiting
Apple's sales in India have actually dropped in the June quarter, but that's reportedly because of supply constraints. Otherwise, sales have been growing for four years.
Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro comes with a variable aperture camera, but new features are not the reason sales are up in India.

The same can't be said for rival manufacturers, though, and particularly not for those making entry-level smartphones. The sales drop for those is said to have been acute since the start of 2026, although no figures were given.
It may not last
If Apple gets the balance of aspirational purchase and zero-interest purchase plans wrong, it could mean the end of the iPhone as a status symbol. Then, too, there can always be a new status symbol.

There won't be one from Samsung, though, as Apple's main smartphone rival has consistently struggled in China. A Chinese rival is more likely, and at times phones by local manufacturers have taken market share from Apple.

If new features are not the priority for customers, then it's hard to predict when a sales bubble might burst. But one reason that Chinese brands have done well has been because of locals favoring them during the US/China trade disputes.

That may well happen again as the new US sanctions against Russia may affect that country's sale of energy to India. Then, too, there are reportedly boardroom disputes at the Tata Group, which is now a major manufacturer of the iPhone.
The Tata Group's iPhone factory was recently accused of contaminating local water supplies and came close to being shut down. Then it was also hit by a hack that exposed confidential Apple documents.
But then India, already a growing manufacturing hub for the iPhone, has recently introduced tax breaks to sweeten Apple's deals there.

And while it has yet to be officially launched, it appears that Apple Pay may finally be coming to India. If so, it's going to be limited to a few banks at first, which could even increase its status as a premium device.

A subset of iPhone 18 Pro Max users in the U.S. are experiencing issues with AT&T; cellular connectivity and/or eSIM provisioning, according to complaints across the MacRumors Forums, Reddit, and the Apple Support Community.
Affected users are unable to connect to the AT&T; network for phone calls, text messages, or data.

Notably, the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the only new iPhone released this month that is equipped with a Qualcomm cellular modem. The smaller iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo are equipped with Apple's C2 modem worldwide, as is the iPhone 18 Pro Max in all other countries. However, it is unclear if this is a contributing factor.
Apple is currently testing iOS 27.0.1, which is expected to be released next week, and hopefully it includes a carrier update that resolves these AT&T; issues.

evidence.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Comes in Four Different Hardware Versions

units.text: iPhone 18 Pro Max Comes in Four Different Hardware Versions

Apple sells four different versions of the iPhone 18 Pro Max depending on where you buy it. While the differences are subtle, they still matter, spanning everything from SIM support to 5G connectivity, modem, and even battery capacity.

The model sold in the U.S., A3473, is eSIM-only and supports both sub-6GHz 5G and faster mmWave networks. It's also the odd one out internally. A teardown by TechInsights confirmed that the U.S. model uses Qualcomm's Snapdragon X80 modem, while every other iPhone 18 Pro Max uses Apple's own C2 modem, as do the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo worldwide. Apple hasn't said why.
A second eSIM-only version, A3716, is sold in Canada, Japan, Mexico, and several Middle Eastern markets, but that model lacks mmWave support.
In most other countries, including the UK and the rest of Europe, Apple sells model A3717. This version retains a physical nano-SIM tray alongside eSIM.
Meanwhile, China gets its own A3718 model with physical nano-SIM cards, and Apple now also allows the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max to be activated there using either eSIM or a physical SIM.

Finally, battery capacity. Regulatory filings indicate the eSIM-only Pro Max models feature larger 5,567mAh batteries, compared to 5,391mAh in models that need space for a physical SIM tray. So a U.S. eSIM-only iPhone 18 Pro Max offers roughly an extra hour of normal use, or two extra hours of video playback.

evidence.discovery_title: Interview: Why Ron Johnson says Apple had no choice but to gamble millions on retail
evidence.raw_lead: Steve Jobs and Ron Johnson were mocked by business and finance press over the Apple Store, and in an interview with AppleInsider, Johnson reveals that if they hadn't opened them, Apple itself would not have survived.
evidence.title: Interview: Why Ron Johnson says Apple had no choice but to gamble millions on retail

units.text: Steve Jobs and Ron Johnson were mocked by business and finance press over the Apple Store, and in an interview with AppleInsider, Johnson reveals that if they hadn't opened them, Apple itself would not have survived.

You've been in an Apple Store, or at least if you haven't, the odds are that there is one near you. These stores are everywhere, they are an unquestioned and unparalleled success, plus Apple has enough money that if a store fails, it isn't the end of the world.

Back in the late 1990s, though, Apple was only slowly climbing back away from what had seemed like a death spiral. It was close to bankruptcy when Steve Jobs returned to the company, and the stories that the iMac and the iPod saved Apple are true.

Yet as great as those devices were, Apple could not get customers to buy them. At that point, they were only really sold in big box retailers alongside PCs that couldn't match what the Mac could do, but invariably beat it on price.
What Jobs saw then was that Apple Stores could be the answer. It was a gamble costing many millions of dollars at a time when Apple couldn't really afford to lose that much.

So the story of the Apple Store is fantastic. It's a slice of Apple history, it's an example of invention and risk taking saving the day. And it's as much the story of how Apple makes products as any account of the iPhone or Mac is.

This is why Ron Johnson's new book, "Shop Different," is significant. There's so much to this story that you will be left wanting more, but the book is the inside man's account of what went right, and what went wrong.
Johnson spoke with William Gallagher for the AppleInsider podcast. Here's A lightly edited and condensed transcript of their conversation.
Speaking with Ron Johnson

WILLIAM GALLAGHER: Actually, I would like, if you don't mind, to just forget everything you've done and leap forward to right now because just as your book is coming out, Apple has had this massive launch, yet we're not going to have queues outside Apple stores anymore. Do you think we're missing out on something now? Have we lost something?

RON JOHNSON: Well, I do. [But] I do think when the iPhone Duo comes out, the stores will be as busy as they've been in years. Because it's been since 2015, really when Apple Watch was announced, that you had a dramatically different form factor for people to check out.
But everyone uses an iPhone. And whether you're gonna buy this new duo or not, you're gonna want to check it out. And the stores will be packed.

Apple's done such a fabulous job since I left. But I loved lines, you know, and Apple got to a point where they just didn't like the idea of having lines outside, but, you know, customers chose to line up. They didn't have to. [It] was an event for them.

We used to see families gather outside and fathers and sons and grandparents and grandsons, and they would stay overnight and we'd bring them water and it was a beautiful thing. It was a beautiful thing, I thought, and the employees loved it. It got energy.
I remember line at our Ginza store in Tokyo went 10 subway stations long - in a typhoon warning. You know, those were the days. Those were the days.
Our very first store outside of the US, Apple Ginza is always such a special place. Thanks for a wonderful visit! pic.twitter.com/h1ZLMhIpA5
— Tim Cook (@tim_cook) December 10, 2019
WG: I know from your book that you saw queues, but did you ever actually join the line to see what it was like?

RJ: Oh, I would walk. I love to go out in the lines. Every day when I was at an opening, I would go out and talk to people in the line, just to get to know them, to understand why they came. Right before the launch, I just walked the line with a couple of other employees to see how long it was and to thank people for coming.

I'll never forget, we opened a store at Shibuya-ku in Tokyo, and we went out. It was a super hot summer day. We walked the line, and then we realised we couldn't get back in time for the opening. So we had to run back and by the time I got there, I was sweating from just being outside in the warm heat. But those were moments that you never forget.

WG: You say in your book that Apple reached out to you, that Steve Jobs's recruiter was the first one to contact you. But as a retail man at that moment, did it seem sensible to you that Apple would want stores?
RJ: Well, I understood why Apple would want stores. In 2000 when I joined Apple, Apple had been a company for 25 years, and the perspective was that Microsoft had won. Microsoft had 95% market share.
Already a block down from the Tokyo Ginza Apple Store and the line for iphoneX is still going https://t.co/OJDIEbp2ZN
— Elise Hu (@elisewho) November 2, 2017

And arguably, Apple had beautiful products and great software and they were a little overpriced or higher price than the PCs, but the market here was way too [small]. And so if you looked at the go to market strategy where you could buy Macs.
Well, in the US, you couldn't buy them at Best Buy or Circuit City, they didn't carry the Mac, and they are the two most popular consumer electronics stores.

So if Apple was going to win, Steve concluded that it had to take the experience directly to the customer. So it had to do its own stores. And I believed it because I was a retail guy and I just brought design to all at Target.

I had this dream. Why does good design have to be expensive? And we did this big design initiative that a lot of people thought was kind of crazy in its own right. But it succeeded. It was fabulous. Customers loved it.
And I figured if we could bring design to Target, we could figure out how to sell a great product like a Mac to customers.
WG: Yes, but Target is a more familiar, more typical retailer with shelves and shelves of products. As you say in the book, Apple had four products or something. So a lot of empty space to fit.

RJ: I was surprised, I honestly was surprised. The night I met Steve, that first interview, after about two hours of chatting, he said, well, do you want to see the product line? And I said, sure. And we walked down to another room, actually the boardroom.
And there were four products on a little credenza. Two [Mac] portables and two desktops. And we were going to build these big, beautiful stores.
Children playing on iMacs in the first Apple Store on the first day. They will now be 25 years old but it's not recorded whether they ever bought a Mac.
But it actually was the opportunity. Because most retail stores back then were just packed with products, and they were almost overwhelming to a customer, right?

And because we had all that space, we could get a lot of products for people to try, [and] we could create all these other services that became important to getting someone to decide to buy a Mac. Theaters and Genius Bars and things like that that ultimately became the support the stores became famous for.
WG: It took a while to get the name Genius Bar, though, I've just learned from your book. What were the other ones you went through?

RJ: Well, Steve wanted to call it the Geek Bar. Because he said, you've been to a bar before, [it can be] kind of fun to go up to a bar. Bartenders are conversational and they can make any drink you want. It's kind of fun. We thought, what if you could get advice for technology, like you're going up to a bar?

That would demystify the fear that a lot of people had of having to talk to someone about technology because it's over people's heads. I told Steve, we're going to get these people who are really good at technology, but they love people and are [good at conversation].
And he said, they don't exist. Everyone who knows technology is kind of geeky. Maybe you call it the geek bar.

But then I'd seen Apple's genius campaign, and I felt like if we called a Genius Bar, People would come out of the woodwork wanting that job. Because who wouldn't want to be the smartest Apple person in every city?
The queues are not completely gone. This is a Shanghai Apple Store so busy that this is the queue just to get in — image credit: Apple
After a minute, Steve, yeah, after a minute, basically called up our general counsel, and said, hey, could you trademark the name Genius Bar? So I knew we had a chance to go do it.

WG: You opened two stores at the same time, but before then, you had this famous warehouse where you were trying things out. It's often been reported that there was a massive change right towards the end, but in your book, you specified that it was around the iMac and that basically it was your fault.
RJ: Well, it was all what happened was we were ready to open our first store and we had spent a lot of time designing it.
Then I had this interesting conversation with Steve because Steve, you know, had been positioning the iMac as one, two, three, you're on the internet. It was the easy getting on the internet.

But we were starting to make these apps, like iMovie, an iPhoto, and I told Steve that this is so interesting. I was still commuting back to Minneapolis on the weekends and [there] I'm in an analogue world. Then in Cupertino. I'm in a digital world all day long and I kind of go between these two things.

And I said, you know, if the Mac's a success, it'll be the center of your digital life. And he came into the executive team meeting the next Monday, and I'm not saying it was solely that conversation, he probably had a lot of conversations about similar things, but he got all excited and stood at the whiteboard and drew a picture.

He goes, "I figured out the future of the Mac, we're going to call it the digital hub. And the Mac will be at the centre of your devices and our software will bring it together and that's how we'll market the Mac."

After I heard that, that night I was thinking about it, I woke up and I thought, well, if Steve's going to market the Mac as the digital hub, our store's [need to do that]. Our store was like any retail store, it was is built around products. We had portables and desktops.

I told Steve, well, maybe we ought to organize a store on movies and music and photos and the things you do. And he got really upset. I mean, it we're going to the warehouse for our weekly design meeting.
And he said, "Ron, do you know how much time I put into the store?" And "I don't know if I had the energy to do another one. So you might be right, but don't bring it up today."

I said, okay. And we would drive together and we rode over in the car and it's perfectly quiet. And we walked into the warehouse and the store was pretty much done. Everything's laid out and Steve looked, everyone's standing there, about 15 people, and he's looking around.
Then he goes, "you know, Ron thinks we've got this store all wrong, and he's right. So I'm going to leave now and you guys can figure it out how."
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube

But then he told a story before he left about everything great he had done, especially with the Pixar movies. He said, "I had to hit the rewind button at some point when I knew it could be better. And it often involved a delay, but you get one chance to do something, so you've got to do it right.
So it took us about six extra months to get the store ready. But we launched and it was a much better store.

The front half of the store [was] about the products. So iBook was here, the PowerBook pro computer was there. We had it spread out like that, with the iMac was in a bay. But we said, no, let's not do that.
Let's have a bay for photography where we put together digital cameras with a Mac, digital cameras with an iBook with each of our products to show how you would do digital photography on a Mac.
And it actually is really interesting because that's what got people to want to buy Macs. Because it was pretty easy to communicate.
They could buy online, but nobody understood how the product could really allow you to do great things with movies and photography and music. And so it became a much more inviting store
WG: Retail space is expensive. Had you already bought the Tyson's corner site before you delayed six months?

RJ: We had already hired all the store leaders, so we had a lot of cost to carry. We had to carry the leases, but it opened up a great opportunity because the Ritz Carlton, who we were inspired by because they delivered the best service in the world in hospitality, invited our first store leaders to go help them open Ritz Carlton hotels.

And so we sent half of the group down to a hotel in Dallas, another half to a hotel, I think, was in Washington, DC, and they spent better part of a week just learning how to launch a hotel. And a lot of the things that the Ritz did from a service perspective, we incorporated into our service strategy.

If you look at the Apple stores, what they're really famous for is the experience you have from an employee [and], how these really smart, nice people take care of things for you. We learned a lot of that from Ritz.
The way to tell that this is a Microsoft promotional photo for its stores is to count the people. There were never this many in real Microsoft Stores - image credit: Microsoft.
So if we had opened on time, not only would we have had an inferior store design, we wouldn't have had the culture ready to go the way we did six months later. So it turned out to be a great delay.
WG: Why did you start by opening two stores? Wouldn't it have been better to try one first and see if it worked?

RJ: The reality is, Steve and I both believed Apple wouldn't work without stores. I had this conviction that a great Apple store in a high traffic location would get traffic and people would buy products.

Then Apple is a global company. At that time, Apple was big in Japan, big in France, big in many of the countries in continental Europe, big in the United States, big in the Canada. And we had to get on with this, you know? So we concluded that we would open 25 stores a year every year.
After four years, you know, it was interesting. We had around 100 stores [and] that's when we opened our Fifth Avenue store.
They were getting bigger and better, but we had the footprint that when Apple launched a great product, wow, everyone could experience that, you know, because we did a really good job.
Our real estate team found all these great sites and we used to get packed stores with these new product launches.
WG: Today, if someone didn't know any of this, they would shrug: 25 stores a year is easy for Apple with its trillions of dollars. But back then, it was a huge and expensive gamble.

RJ: When Steve came back three years before the stores, we had 30 days of cash. And, you know, Tim [Cook] did a lot of things on inventory management to generate cash and Bill Gates wrote a $100 million check, as you recall, you know, to help Apple stay afloat.

Steve understood how important cash was. Steve never delivered a dividend during his time as CEO, he never bought back stock. He had been too close to the edge [so] he wanted to protect all the money Apple had.

When Tim came in, Tim had a different approach to the balance sheet and a big part of one of his good financial moves was buying back stock all the time, you know, which helped the stock price did a lot of benefits.
But Steve was [always saying] let's protect our cash, you never know where you need it. We might have a rainy day. You just never know. So it was a big bet, but it was the only bet Apple could make.
WG: You mentioned the Fifth Avenue store, it's an amazing store, and a fantastic location, except it isn't on Fifth Avenue. It's underground. Who's made idea was that?

RJ: We always said to our teams, when I was there, never sell the customer more than they need. We spent a lot of time asking customers, what are you going to use your product for, and we get them to the right memory configure it, the right model for them.

I have had amazing experiences over the last three months in a variety of stores around the world, and that energy's back, that love of the customers back. I really feel a huge difference [and] I am really proud of what the stores are doing right now.

units.text: Exclusive: First Look at HomePod Mini 2 in Three New Colors
Apple's new HomePod mini will share the same design as the original model and come in five colors, MacRumors has found.

The information originates from Apple's own code (spotted by MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris) and shows clear product images of the new models in all of their colors. The above image contains Apple's own icons, which specifically refer to a "‌HomePod mini‌ 2."

The new ‌HomePod mini‌ will come in green, pink, blue, white, and black. The current model comes in yellow, orange, blue, white, and midnight. The new blue is slightly lighter than the current offering.
We are not sharing the exact details of the files, but their presence in Apple's code suggests that the product is likely to launch soon.

Apple announced the original ‌HomePod mini‌ in October 2020 for $99. Available initially in white and space gray, the 3.3-inch speaker features a fabric-covered spherical design and a backlit touch surface for playback and volume controls. Its S5 chip powers computational audio, while a full-range driver, two passive radiators, and an acoustic waveguide deliver 360-degree sound. It also offers Siri, smart home control, multiroom audio, stereo pairing with a second ‌HomePod mini‌, and Intercom messages between Apple devices. Apple later raised the price to $129.

Apple has been rumored to be working on a new ‌HomePod mini‌ model for several years. A new chip is almost certain to come to the device, along with support for Siri AI. It is expected to launch before the end of 2026.

units.text: Apple today revealed the first eight shows coming to its new Apple Music Hall in London, with Elton John set to kick things off next week. Here are the details.
Elton John to headline first Apple Music Hall show
Earlier this week, Apple unveiled the Apple Music Hall, a new concert venue in the famous Battersea Power Station in London, where the company also has an office and a store.

Apple Music Hall will hold up to 600 people, with performances also livestreamed globally through Apple Music. Artists will also walk away with a finished Spatial Audio recording, a broadcast-ready mix, and multicamera video.
When Apple first announced Apple Music Hall, the company said it would soon unveil the first artists set to perform at the venue.
Today, Apple confirmed the first eight shows, kicking off with Elton John next week. Here’s the full lineup:
Elton John — September 28
Baby Keem — October 2
Skye Newman — October 7
Troye Sivan — October 13
Arlo Parks — October 22
Burna Boy — October 29
Chase & Status — November 26
Charli xcx — December 2

Some of the artists also have a long history with Apple Music. Elton John, for instance, has hosted his weekly “Rocket Hour” radio show since Apple Music launched in 2015, while Charli xcx previously hosted five seasons of her own show, “The Candy Shop,” on Beats 1.
Back to the concerts, Apple says “tickets for Elton John, Baby Keem & Skye Newman will go on sale Monday 28th September at 9AM BST,” while “all remaining shows will go on sale at a later date.”
For more information on tickets and availability, follow this link.
Apple Music requires an active subscription. You can sign up for $11.99 per month, with 1 month free, or as part of the Apple One bundle.

evidence.title: How to Check Your Mac's Manufacture Date in macOS 27

units.text: If you installed macOS 27 Golden Gate, here's a way to find out when your Mac was manufactured. Apple has restored access to information that effectively disappeared when it randomized its serial numbers a few years ago.

On your Mac, go to System Settings ➝ General ➝ About, then click "Regulatory Certification" under the System Report button. The certificate will show with a new "Date of Manufacture" field at the bottom.

You used to be able to decode the serial number on an Apple device to find out when and where it was made. That changed in 2021, when Apple began adopting randomized serial numbers without encoded manufacturing details.
That left owners of newer Macs with no similarly straightforward way to determine when their machine was made – until macOS 27 arrived.

The spot was made by MacRumors forum member pdfu. Another forum member said that the displayed date they saw on their certificate corresponded to their Mac's logic board rather than the date the complete machine was assembled. That logic board had been replaced though, suggesting that's where the date of manufacture is stored.
The regulatory certification first appeared during the macOS 27 beta cycle and it hasn't, to our knowledge, been highlighted by Apple.

evidence.title: AirPods just got a long-requested feature in new software update - 9to5Mac

units.text: While it was overshadowed by release of iOS 27, Apple also released a new software update for AirPods this month. The update brings a long-requested feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.
AirPods software details
The latest AirPods firmware build number is 9A350 for AirPods 5 and 9A348 for the other models below. The update is available for the following AirPods models:
AirPods Pro 3
AirPods 4
AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation
AirPods 5
AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case
AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C)
AirPods Max 2

Apple says that AirPods firmware updates are automatically installed while your AirPods are charging and within Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac that’s connected to WiFi. You can check the firmware version of your AirPods in the Settings app on iPhone.
Custom EQ comes to AirPods
Once you install the AirPods firmware update, you’ll see a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.
You now have more control over how your AirPods sound thanks to the new custom EQ controls. In the Settings app, you can adjust the lows, mids, and highs of your AirPods sound.

“AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls,” Apple explains. “If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.”
While adjusting the custom EQ settings, you can play a song from Apple Music right in the Settings app to hear the adjustments in real time.

This isn’t the most advanced equalizer feature out there. It’s a basic, three-band system. Still, it’s a long-awaited AirPods feature that Apple has finally given users—even if most will likely stick with the default levels.

You can find the new custom EQ feature in the AirPods section of the Settings app under the “Audio and Routing” menu. The feature is available on all AirPods with an H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.
Other iOS 27 features for AirPods
Here are the other new AirPods features for iOS 27:

Settings app redesign: In iOS 27, Apple has redesigned the AirPods interface in the Settings app. The controls have been reorganized, with separate menus for Hearing Health, Find My, Live Translation, and more.
Adaptive Audio slider: In the Settings app, you now have a slider to further fine-tune Adaptive Audio mode.
GymKit: While GymKit has been around for years, it’s always required an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac explains, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding in the Find My app on Apple Watch to locate AirPods Pro 3.
Siri AI: When paired to a compatible iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.
Wrap up
What new AirPods features are you most excited to try? Are you going to try the new custom EQ feature? Let us know down in the comments.

units.text: Apple TV has been called “the new HBO” for its focus on quality over quantity. But recently, the streamer has starting ramping its lineup of shows I want to watch, and I can’t keep up.
Apple TV’s quality and quantity have ramped up as streamer hits new stride
I’ve subscribed to Apple TV since it first debuted in 2019, and the streamer has typically had 1-2 shows on at a time that I’ve wanted to watch.
This kind of output resembles HBO, which has built its brand creating fewer, but generally higher-quality shows than most competitors.
In the last couple years though, Apple’s output has been slowly growing, and at the same time its batting average has arguably improved too.
The result? Apple has too many good shows on right now, and I can’t keep up.
Currently airing every week on Apple TV are new episodes of:
Ted Lasso, one of my favorite shows
Slow Horses, another all-time best Apple series
Dark Matter, a sci-fi series I loved the first season of, yet haven’t started the second
Brothers, a new half-hour comedy with Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson that looks fun
Last Seen, a new thriller I’ve heard great things about but haven’t watched
plus Women in Blue and Knife Edge, both of which I might watch in a slower season but right now they’re low priorities

I’m excited to dive into Dark Matter, as season 1 made it one of my favorite sci-fi shows just behind Severance and Pluribus. But it’s been hard to find time to start season 2. And I’m always up for a comfort watch half-hour comedy, so Brothers is in the queue.
I love crime thrillers and dramas involving family, so Last Seen looks very much like my kind of show. But I haven’t started it yet, despite Stephen King’s endorsement.

Two observations about LAST SEEN, 4 episodes in (Apple+): 1–It's a fantastic show, and 2–I see no good resolution for the families involved. Or for Sarah, who is played beautifully by Chloe Jean Lourdes.
— Stephen King (@StephenKing) September 24, 2026
And these are only the shows currently airing.

I’m still not caught up on Silo season 3, and haven’t even started Sugar season 2 despite great reviews and being a fan of the show. I could watch more on Apple if I ignored other streamers, but other shows elsewhere are keeping me busy too.
October is right around the corner too, and Apple has a whopping seven new TV shows and movies premiering—the most I can remember in a single month.
All this to say, I’m really pleased that Apple TV is doing so well. It won more Emmys than HBO this year for a reason.
What’s your view on Apple TV’s current and recent shows? Let us know in the comments.
Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month, or you can get it discounted through the Apple One bundle.

evidence.title: 共事约 11 年：苹果零售总设计师约翰逊谈乔布斯理念“不急于求成”

units.text: IT之家 9 月 26 日消息，科技媒体 Business Insider 今天（9 月 26 日）发布博文，报道称在新书发布会上，苹果零售“总设计师”罗恩 · 约翰逊（Ron Johnson）表示，史蒂夫 · 乔布斯留给他的核心教训是“不急于求成”（Don't be in a hurry）。
IT之家查询公开资料，约翰逊出生于 1959 年，于 2000 年被史蒂夫 · 乔布斯聘请，担任苹果零售业务高级副总裁，负责从零搭建 Apple Store，可谓是苹果零售体系真正的“总设计师”，他和乔布斯共事约 11 年。
约翰逊最新发布新书《另辟蹊径：零售业如何揭示苹果的天才之处》，在媒体采访活动中，约翰逊表示乔布斯留给他的最重要教训是“不要着急”，这一理念成为约翰逊日后管理哲学的核心锚点，并相信“大胆的愿景无法强求或仓促实现，需要时间才能逐渐显现”。
约翰逊回忆，乔布斯工作时全神贯注，不随身携带手机。下次会面时，乔布斯能完整复述上周讨论的所有内容。这种高度专注力贯穿其日常工作与决策。
乔布斯领导下的苹果产品发布策略体现这一理念。苹果在 2001 年推出 iPod，但直到 2007 年才发布 iPhone。约翰逊称，乔布斯希望 iPod 做到极致，之后才“有资格”开发手机。
约翰逊负责构建苹果零售网络时，外界普遍认为实体零售因电商兴起而走向衰落。他坚持推进计划，最终苹果门店大获成功。约翰逊离开苹果后出任 JCPenney 首席执行官。他将乔布斯的“不要着急”理念带入新岗位，并在多年后仍铭记这一教训。

units.text: Not everyone knows this (and I won’t even pretend that I did), but Apple publishes remarkably detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of its devices to help accessory makers design products around them. Here are the details.
Apple hardware, mapped in great detail
For almost 30 years, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources for interesting content on (and off) the internet that I would most certainly have never discovered otherwise.
A few days ago, he published this post, linking to Apple’s Dimensional Drawings section inside the Accessories area of its developer website.

In a nutshell, this is a repository of incredibly detailed technical drawings of what currently amounts to 96 devices, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and the AirPods 5.
The list also includes products like the MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, as well as accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and even the Apple Vision Pro’s ZEISS Optical Inserts.

Each document includes precise measurements for everything from the device’s overall dimensions and curves to its buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers, and connectors, along with detailed keepout zones and instructions showing where certain materials should not be placed.

While these documents are meant for accessory makers, they’re also likely to appeal to anyone with even a mild interest in hardware, industrial design, or simply the kind of attention to detail that generally draws people to Apple products in the first place.
For Apple’s Dimensional Drawings, follow this link. And if you don’t already, make sure to start following kottke.org.

units.text: Apple has a big October ahead, with several major hardware and software launches coming. Here’s everything to expect from Apple in October.
iPhone Duo launches October 23
iPhone Duo is confirmed to arrive in users’ hands in October. Pre-orders open Friday, October 16 and the first units deliver on October 23.
Apple’s first foldable model might be limited in supply. However, iPhone Duo is launching in lots of countries simultaneously, which could be a good sign for availability. Per Apple:

Customers in more than 70 countries and regions, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, India, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Türkiye, the UAE, the UK, the U.S., and Vietnam, will be able to pre-order iPhone Duo beginning at 5 a.m. PT on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23. iPhone Duo will be available in 28 other countries and regions beginning Friday, October 30.
If iPhone Duo supply was expected to be significantly lower than anticipated demand, it’s unlikely Apple would launch the product in close to 100 countries and regions right away.
Read more: Apple unveils foldable iPhone Duo
Hardware rumors: New Macs, Home products, and iPad mini
Apple reportedly has a lot more new hardware products launching in October too. We’re expecting new Macs, Home products, and an upgraded iPad mini. Here’s what’s rumored:
Touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra: All-new design for high-end MacBook with OLED, more
M6 iMac: Powerful chip and new color options
M6 MacBook Pro: Update for 14-inch base MacBook Pro
New Apple TV 4K: A19 or A19 Pro chip, Siri AI, new Siri Remote
HomePad: New home hub with built-in touchscreen
HomePod mini 2: More powerful chip, audio upgrades, more
iPad mini: OLED display, A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip

Two standout products include the first touchscreen Mac, which could be branded MacBook Pro or Ultra, and the long-expected home hub ‘HomePad.’ Everything else will be smaller updates to existing products.
Software launches: iOS 27.1 and iOS 27.2, more
Apple has confirmed that iPhone Duo will run on iOS 27.1 when it launches in October.
It’s speculated that 27.1 will be Duo-exclusive. However, it might come to other iPhones too, but only include bug fixes or security updates while the majority of changes are for Apple’s foldable.

Normally we would expect more features in iOS 27.1, but in an unusual move, iOS 27.2 is already in testing and is also expected to arrive in October. As a result, iOS 27.2 is likely intended for all iPhones while 27.1 is primarily for iPhone Duo.
New features in iOS 27.2 so far include:
Profiles for the Apple TV app come to iPhone and iPad
Dual Capture feature available for Group FaceTime calls
Siri AI expands to several new languages
New features for Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, and more might be coming too

When iOS 27 launched, Apple confirmed that Siri AI “will expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish next month.“ Since that language expansion is included in iOS 27.2, we’re expecting both 27.1 and 27.2 to arrive before October ends.
The iOS 27.2 beta also includes an all-new Health app with Apple Intelligence features, but it’s expected to be removed from the shipping version and return in iOS 27.3 later this year instead.

units.text: 快科技9月26日消息，据财联社消息，美国圣地亚哥联邦陪审团近日裁定，苹果公司因侵犯Taction科技公司的振动技术相关专利，需支付超57亿美元的赔偿，该专利技术被应用于多款iPhone和Apple Watch产品中。
陪审团认定苹果侵犯了Taction的两项触觉反馈专利，但裁定该侵权行为不构成蓄意侵权。Taction于2021年就该专利对苹果提起诉讼，涉案专利描述的是“可通过触觉感知的低频振动触觉换能器”技术。
据公开报道梳理，这起案件的审理过程一波三折。
2021年，Taction正式递交诉状，直指苹果Taptic Engine触觉引擎，也就是 iPhone、Apple Watch 上广泛使用的振动模块，落入其两项专利保护范围，主张苹果直接侵权、同时诱导侵权，要求苹果承担相应赔偿责任。
苹果随后进行应诉，不仅否认侵权，还提起反诉，同时向美国专利商标局提交四份多方复审申请，请求宣告Taction涉案专利全部权利要求无效，试图从根源废掉对方专利基础。
2023年，苹果曾成功说服法官驳回该案。Taction就此向美国联邦巡回上诉法院提起上诉。
2025年，联邦巡回上诉法院作出裁决，裁定当初驳回案件所依据的一项不成文要求，不当剥夺了Taction使用部分专家证言的权利，推翻下级法院的简易判决，将案件发回圣地亚哥地方法院重审。
值得注意的是，公开报道还披露，Taction这家企业本身并不消费电子硬件产品，本次诉讼背后有第三方诉讼融资机构提供资金支持，苹果在庭审前期就曾试图挖掘、披露Taction与诉讼资本之间的关联，双方对抗强度很高。
案件发回重审之后，本案进入陪审团庭审阶段。经过两天的陪审团评议，最终给出57亿美元的赔偿裁决。
陪审团同时明确，苹果不属于蓄意侵权，按照美国专利法，该结论意味着 Taction无法申请三倍惩罚性赔偿，本次57亿美元为基础侵权赔偿额度。
